what: One decision per kind of upstream file, first match wins. `*` matches anything, `/` included. A file no entry matches is HELD: reported, never copied. Dispositions: ours (Ultron's version always wins; upstream's is read, not applied), take (apply upstream's change after tests), merge (by hand), later (wanted, in a planned slice), parked (known, not copied), rejected. Add `reconciled` (a full upstream commit id) once a file has been brought up to that upstream version, so the next comparison measures from there.

entries.reason: They steer agents and models, or hold the licence terms. Upstream's version is read and never applied (DECISIONS.md section 8); anything worth keeping is written into Ultron's own file by hand.
Ultron's safety, launch and CI files. The in-app agent may not edit them, and an upstream version is never taken in their place.
Ultron's own readme. What a new Mark adds is credited by hand in docs/UPSTREAM_RESEARCH.md; the attribution paragraph stays.
Ultron's read, lock and write rules for the settings file win (the file is never replaced by one made from a failed read). New upstream settings are ported by hand, through this file only.

The owner chose to adopt upstream's window layer last, after the back-end features. Ultron's own window work lives in ui.py: the Tools panel, multi-provider setup, the confirm banner the self-change gate uses, and the proof gate and three test files read ui.py as text.
Nothing in upstream's own program imports them (checked at 752ff61). They open sockets, deploy to a server over SSH and talk to Telegram. Not copied until upstream wires them in and the owner agrees.
Planned slice: background tasks and deep research. Ships switched off, and reuses Ultron's public-address guard instead of keeping upstream's second copy.
Planned slice: routines. It must satisfy exclusions E1 to E3 in EXCLUSIONS.json: no news on open, no news watch, nothing that runs tools by itself at launch.
